articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang built the company that powers AI. Now Nvidia must find a way forward without him
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang built the company that powers AI. Now Nvidia must find a way forward without him
articles.content_orig:

Over three decades, Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang helped propel the chipmaker’s rise into one of the world’s most valuable and resilient companies, leading the business through near-death and periods of reinvention.
Now the self-described “battlefield CEO” faces a personal crisis that will test a roughly $4-trillion Silicon Valley powerhouse that has become the face of the artificial intelligence revolution.
Over the weekend, the 63-year-old tech billionaire and married father of two sent an apology to his employees, admitting he had an affair and is hoping to win back trust. Nvidia’s board announced it is launching an investigation after allegations surfaced that Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
“Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence,” Huang said in the note to employees.
The board said it doesn’t believe the relationship compromised Nvidia’s secrets or national security. China has dismissed the allegations as an unsubstantiated “smear” campaign against the country.
The revelations, though, rattled Silicon Valley and Washington, where federal lawmakers have called for an investigation into accusations that China targeted the powerful tech mogul. The scandal also comes as the U.S. competes with China in the AI race, raising more scrutiny over Nvidia’s business with the country.
Nvidia launched the investigation after the New York Times first reported in late October that American intelligence agencies found that Huang developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen that was passing on intelligence to Beijing. The woman, Alice Huang, worked as an executive for Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which is one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed didn’t respond to a request for comment but told the New York Times that it “cannot respond to a media trial and welcomes formal, evidence-based investigation.”
On Monday, Nvidia’s share price fell about 5% to roughly $177  as investors expressed anxiety about how the scandal will affect the company’s future.
Though analysts say it’s unlikely that Huang will be ousted as chief executive and Nvidia will probably remain a dominant AI player, the drama has raised questions about the company’s succession plans and how it will affect the chipmaker’s competition with rivals.
“He’s become a tech celebrity, which has shown to be both a blessing and a curse for companies. His conduct could raise questions about his judgment and potentially undermine some of the confidence he’s built among investors, customers and developers,” said Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst.
Over the years, Huang, who’s known for donning a black leather jacket, has shown he’s a visionary, dealmaker and politically savvy, forging strong ties with President Trump. Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at Technalysis Research, said that Nvidia will likely be around for decades, but that the scandal is shining a spotlight on who will succeed Huang.
That will be hard to top. Huang’s two children work for Nvidia.
“He’s been able to turn that big personality and vision and dealmaking into this point where he is arguably the leader, certainly of the hardware side of the tech industry,” O’Donnell said. “Everything he says matters and every company wants to do deals with Nvidia.”
Huang is no stranger to navigating through turmoil, and as a leader he’s emphasized the importance of character and resilience.
Born in Taiwan, Huang spent some time in Thailand before his family sent him to the United States, where he attended a religious reform school. There, he told news outlets, he was bullied for being Chinese and even scrubbed toilets.
He met his future wife, Lori, at Oregon State University, where they were studying electrical engineering.
Huang, along with engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, founded Nvidia in 1993 at a Denny’s diner in San José,  where they envisioned building a computer chip to improve video game graphics.
In its early days, Nvidia contracted with game company Sega, but it almost went out of business by betting on the wrong approach for building graphics chips. Huang laid off employees and convinced Sega to invest $5 million in the company, avoiding bankruptcy, according to an interview he did on “How I Built This with Guy Raz.”
The company created specialized computer chips that would not only be used for gaming but also for cryptocurrency mining, AI model training and robotics.
Nvidia also partnered with OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, early, before people turned more to AI to automate tasks. In 2016, Huang hand-delivered Nvidia’s new supercomputer to OpenAI. As ChatGPT became more popular, Nvidia benefited from the AI boom.
“He’s been on the cutting edge of all of this for a very long time, and then the rest of the world kind of caught up with what he saw and what the industry was doing, and now of course we are where we are,” O’Donnell said.
As other tech leaders have called for a slowdown of the AI race, Huang has called for speeding up AI innovation, stating it could help improve safety. Computers, he said, are just software and not conscious.
Even as Nvidia’s prominence has grown, Huang has told media outlets he still worries the company could go out of business, though he says he’s stepped up in times of crisis.
“The perfect day is [when] we are in trouble, and you just create the worst possible condition. And Jensen, we need you to come and help us think through this,” Huang said in an interview on “How I Built This with Guy Raz.”
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Wong also covered politics and education for the Statesman Journal in Salem, Ore. A fter more than 40 years of marriage, Lori Huang may be mulling the possibility of joining one very exclusive group: the tech billionaire ex-wives’ club.
Jensen Huang’s notoriously private wife is yet to speak publicly about his betrayal after the Nvidia co-founder admitted in a letter to staff last week that he had an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy in a “honey trap” plot, before news of a second alleged affair with a married employee came to light Wednesday evening.
Huang resigned Thursday morning as CEO of the chipmaking giant that is spearheading the AI revolution.
The scandal has seen Lori Huang thrust into the spotlight, joining other illustrious women like Melinda French Gates and MacKenzie Scott, who experienced similar ordeals at the hands of their ex-husbands, Microsoft founder Bill Gates and Amazon mogul Jeff Bezos.
Now speculation is mounting as to whether 65-year-old Lori Huang will join the club of exes, acerbically dubbed by journalist Tina Brown as the “female cohort who get the billions, without an egomaniacal man attached.”
Lori Huang is the co-trustee of family trusts that hold nearly 669 million in Nvidia shares, according to Fortune . While there is no indication she has filed for divorce, if she did initiate proceedings against her 63-year-old husband - ranked the eighth-richest man in the world - she would be in line for at least $75 billion, according to Forbes .
When Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates divorced in 2021 after 27 years of marriage, her settlement, while never publicly disclosed, was estimated at around $25 billion. Scott, Bezos’ ex-wife, settled for $38 billion when they divorced in 2019 after 25 years of marriage.
Since then, the women have given away billions of dollars to philanthropic causes.
Aside from their billions, philanthropy is something the women have in common. Lori Huang is the president of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation, and, like her, the nonprofit maintains a low profile.
The Huangs’ foundation, which held $9 billion in assets in 2024, was featured in an Inside Philanthropy report titled “Meet the Black Box Billionaires: Are These America’s Most Secretive Megadonors?” Among its beneficiaries are the San Francisco Opera and universities but the nonprofit steers clear of donating to political causes, according to the New York Times.
Another commonality is that French Gates, Scott and Lori Huang have all played an integral role in the success of their husbands’ businesses.
“Every moment of Nvidia, she was there,” Huang said in a May interview with Asian network CNA . “She’s been part of Nvidia every step of the way.”
The couple met when Lori Huang, then Lori Mills, was one of only three female students in Huang’s electrical engineering class at Oregon State University in the early 1980s. The competition among the 200 male students for the women’s attention was fierce, he recalled in a 2023 New Yorker interview .
Despite the odds (Huang said he looked like he was about 12 years old), six months of bugging Lori Mills to do homework with him every weekend paid off. He worked up the courage to ask her out on a date, and the college sweethearts went on to marry in 1985.
“I tried to impress her—not with my looks, of course, but with my strong capability to complete homework,” he told the New Yorker.
The couple moved to Silicon Valley after they wed and worked as microchip designers. Lori Huang, also a talented engineer, at one point was earning more than her husband, he told the New Yorker. She put her career on hold to raise their two children, Spencer and Madison, and so her husband could co-launch Nvidia, which he did in 1993 from a Denny’s. He recently said the sacrifice of her own career was “the gift that she gave me.”
“Lori took care of everything and I don’t remember her complaining one time,” Huang recalled in May on the How I Built It podcast.
As Nvidia took off and the company’s wealth boomed, Lori Huang was a constant, quiet presence while her husband took center stage at conferences and state dinners.
“Aside from Lori, I don't think anyone has been to every conference,” Huang told CNA. “And she's been to every conference, every speech.”
Huang apologized to his wife and their two children in a statement released November 8, in which he admitted he was unfaithful. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said, asking for privacy for his family. The couple’s children both work at Nvidia.
“My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do,” he said. “Please give them privacy.”
The Independent has contacted Nvidia for comment.
Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to decide Huang’s fate at the company after a second allegation of an extramarital relationship with a senior corporate subordinate emerged. Huang’s position clearly became untenable, forcing his resignation, and the company’s stock plunged 10 percent Thursday morning following the announcement.
The future of the power couple’s marriage, meanwhile, is unclear.
“It’s good to have someone in your life who unconditionally believes in you, who believes you’re doing your best,” Huang said in a 2024 magazine article with his alma mater. “You need people like that, and Lori’s always been that person for me — ever since I was 18, she was there believing in me and knowing I could do it.”
“Even when I had self-doubts, she didn’t,” he added.

articles.title_zh: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang had ‘intimate relationship’ with second employee, Reuters reports
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday.
CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news.
The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release.
Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted.
After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy.
Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future.
Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China.
President Trump lamented the "horrible thing" that happened to Huang in an interview conducted hours after his close corporate ally resigned as Nvidia's CEO.
Trump referenced Huang after telling conservative commentator Hugh Hewitt that the U.S. would be in "bad shape" if it lost its edge in artificial intelligence.
"I've seen it. I study it. I'm genetically blessed. I have an uncle that was probably considered the number one professor in the history of MIT for 51 years," Trump said.
"He was there, and he got the science award, the same award that I gave to Elon [Musk], and you know, I gave them out last week. We gave it to Google. We gave it to a lot of great people ... we gave it to Jensen," he said.
"Frankly, that was a little before. But what a horrible thing that is! That's so sad to see that happen," Trump said. "But my uncle got the same award from Ronald Reagan. They presented it to me when when I was there last week, and it was sort of something. So I do have, I think, an inclination. I'm a believer in that, you know."
The woman at the center of Jensen Huang's spy-sex scandal may have owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Huawei, Nvidia's biggest competitor in Beijing, according to findings from private intelligence firm Tesari shared exclusively with CNBC .
Alice Huang was described as a top executive at Singaporean tech company Megaspeed in initial reporting from The New York Times revealing U.S. officials had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Jensen Huang on Sunday copped to an extramarital affair with an unnamed woman, following numerous additional reports about his close relationship with Alice Huang.
The connections uncovered by Tesari may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the ousted Nvidia chief , and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition.
Click here to read the full report.
— Eamon Javers and Kevin Breuninger
Two of Huang's kids, Madison and Spencer Huang, work at Nvidia. So does Madison's husband, Nico Caprez.
Caprez has risen quickly through the ranks, becoming vice president of global AI infrastructure in January, after joining Nvidia as a corporate development manager in 2024. He was previously an alpine skier and consultant with Boston Consulting Group, and met the CEO's daughter in business school.
Madison joined Nvidia as an intern in 2020 after training as a professional chef, then obtaining a Masters of Business Administration from the London Business school. She serves as a senior director of product marketing for the company's robotics division.
Spencer also works in robotics, serving as the director of product management. He joined Nvidia in 2022 as a product manager in the company's Isaac Sim Cloud division after obtaining an undergraduate degree from Columbia College Chicago and an MBA from New York University's Stern School of Business.
In an all-hands meeting last year, Jensen Huang was asked by employees about nepotism. In a recording of this meeting heard by CNBC, he said that hiring children of Nvidia employees "is a good idea if it's done properly, if it's done on merits." He said he was proud of his kids, and added that children of Nvidia executives working at the company were "even better than their parents."
— Lora Kolodny and Isabel O'Brien
Huang had an "intimate relationship" with a second Nvidia employee, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.
A day earlier, The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of health care. Huang on Sunday admitted to one affair following reports of his intimacy with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, reportedly believed by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
Reuters is not naming the second employee. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Jensen Huang's rise, becoming a "monarch" that was essentially "co-branded so that you can't separate" the CEO from the company, was a corporate governance problem, according to Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at Yale School of Management.
"There are a lot of times [corporate boards] are beholden," Sonnenfeld told CNBC's Morgan Brennan on "Morning Call." "They're smitten by the CEO; kind of idolatry."
Nvidia's board reflects that. Prior to his exit on Thursday, Huang was one of 11 members of the board, which had no chair. None of Nvidia's 10 other board members are current or former S&P 500 CEOs. On average, they've been on the board for 15 years.
Across the S&P 500, the average tenure of an independent director is 7.8 years and roughly one in every four directors is a former CEO, according to 2025 data from the Conference Board . Sonnenfeld said "no one was equipped to step in."
"Somebody needs to ask some questions, and that's what's missing here," he said.
Rep. Bill Huizenga of Michigan, Vice Chair of the House Financial Services Committee and a Republican, said it would be "helpful" if Commerce Department Secretary Howard Lutnick testified to Congress in public, in the wake of reports that he stalled a crackdown of firms routing Nvidia chips to China by President Donald Trump .
"They have not been as cooperative as they should be. They have not been as transparent with Congress, much less I think others within that system," Huizenga said of the Commerce Department Thursday. "I want to hear from them a commitment and a recommitment to national security and making sure that these very important technologies and pieces of equipment and chips and other things aren't falling into the wrong hands."
Huizenga told CNBC the Bureau of Industry and Security, a subagency of Commerce that handles export controls, needs to take Congressional concerns about the export of Nvidia chips to China seriously.
"The notion of being able to slow this down and be more selective is actually a positive thing, and what I mean by [that is] not slowing down the technology, but slowing down that transfer of technology," he said.
The Financial Service

articles.title_orig: Home sales in worst slump since the aftermath of the Great Recession
articles.title_zh: Home sales in worst slump since the aftermath of the Great Recession
articles.content_orig:
Sales of previously owned homes in the US have hit the lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates hover above 7 percent.
The National Association of Realtors (NAR) said on Thursday that home sales dropped 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units. That was the lowest level since August 2010.
“Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023. As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010,” said NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun.
He said, “It is just a tough market for buyers and sellers.”
“Sales decreased by 8.8 percent year-over-year,” the NAR report found. “Month-over-month sales declined in the Midwest, South and West and held steady in the Northeast. Year-over-year sales declined in all four regions.”
The home sales used in the report are counted at the closing of a contract and are a look at previously occupied ones. October’s sales likely reflected contracts signed in August and September.
“Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation,” said the report.
First-time buyers accounted for just 29 percent of home purchases last month, down from 31 percent in September and 32 percent in October last year, NAR said. First-time buyers have historically made up closer to 40 percent of home sales.
The US housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates increased from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied US homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low. Yun expects home sales this year will likely end up lower than in 2025.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.33 percent in October, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, more commonly known as Freddie Mac, up from 6.86 percent in September and 6.25 percent one year ago.
The rate, however, averaged 7.18 percent last week, down from 7.24 percent in the previous week.
Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans.
Until the past few weeks, mortgage rates had been on the rise since late February, when the US war with Iran began, pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher. The run-up in rates also reflected heightened bond market volatility, which led to rising yields on US Treasuries.

articles.title_orig: Putin takes hard line in US talks as Ukraine says Starlink disrupted again
articles.title_zh: Putin takes hard line in US talks as Ukraine says Starlink disrupted again
articles.content_orig:
Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

articles.title_orig: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
articles.title_zh: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
articles.content_orig:
Alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang may have simultaneously owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Nvidia's biggest competitor in China, Huawei, while she was in business with Nvidia and also reportedly having a romantic affair with its ousted CEO Jensen Huang .
The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei was first discovered by analysts at private intelligence firm Tesari. The firm exclusively shared its findings with CNBC. Tesari provides intelligence research to private companies and the U.S. government.
This previously unreported entanglement was first uncovered by the research firm which uses artificial intelligence to collect evidence and specializes in national security investigations around the world. The connections may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the CEO and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition. Jensen Huang has acknowledged having an affair, though the precise timing of his relationship with Alice Huang is unknown.
The mysterious saga of Alice Huang involves a tangle of interlocking corporations and transactions that show her connection to entities that ultimately provided computing power to Huawei in China.
Huawei is known as a Chinese government "state champion" in the technology and telecommunications sectors, meaning it receives enormous financial support from the government in Beijing so it can lower prices and undercut global competitors. It is considered a key part of the Chinese government's push for global technical dominance and is closely linked to the Chinese Communist Party.
Businesses connected to Alice Huang were linked with supplying Nvidia computing power to Huawei, according to documents reviewed by CNBC, around the same time she and Jensen Huang were first publicly seen together in December 2023.
In 2024, Nvidia said Huawei was a top competitor , specifically in artificial intelligence chips including graphics processing units, central processing units and networking chips.
"This activity, which surfaced through our analysis of Alice's network, warrants a national security and [technology] counterproliferation investigation," said Brian Andersen, Tesari's vice president for national security applications and a former supervisory special agent with Homeland Security Investigations.
If the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry Security and Homeland Security Investigations found evidence that anyone transferred "controlled equipment" to Huawei without authorization, potential charges might include include export-control violations, conspiracy and smuggling, Andersen said.
The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei is so convoluted that analysts at Tesari told CNBC that based on their previous investigative experience, they suspect it was designed to deliberately obscure the relationship.
Nvidia and Huawei did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment. Jensen Huang did not respond to a voicemail left on a mobile phone. Alice Huang could not be reached.
According to Chinese corporate records and media reports compiled by Tesari and provided to CNBC, Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le and who according to documents at the time was based in Hong Kong, in 2019 sold a cloud business she owned called Osmanthus to a Chinese gaming company called 7Road. A subsidiary of 7Road, which was based in Singapore, was spun off as "Megaspeed" in 2023 . Megaspeed would go on to become a key Nvidia customer, helping facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms, The Information reported Tuesday.
As early as 2016, Alice Huang had also become a co-owner of a financial firm known as Shanghai Hexi , which heavily invests in tech and data centers.In 2021, Hexi in turn acquired 27 percent of a company called Shanghai Century Longteng, a data center developer, which Hexi held until 2024 . That firm owned a controlling 50.1 percent stake in a data center facility called Shenzhen Yifeng Technology Co., Ltd. in mainland China.
The key customer of that data center was Huawei Cloud , the Shenzhen, China-based subsidiary of Huawei Technologies.
In addition, Alice Huang's firm Hexi guaranteed the loans required to finance the Shenzhen data center, which did business with Huawei.
Hexi did not immediately respond to a message via its LinkedIn page sent outside of normal business hours.
CNBC translated corporate records and Chinese news articles in Mandarin that Tesari provided.
It's not clear if the Shenzhen data center was able to acquire Nvidia GPUs, but its majority owner began purchasing the chips in 2023 . That company is known as Zhejiang Century Huatong Group and is a business partner of Alice Huang's Hexi through their joint ownership of Century Longteng.
That made Alice Huang a part owner of a data center providing computing power to Huawei. And that was happening at around the same time the first known sightings came of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang in public together.
And that raises the question of why Huawei, which has access to Chinese made chips, would need to rent computing power from an outside entity.
Hexi exited its stake in the data center development company in 2024, but individuals within Alice Huang's network are still connected to the Shenzhen data center. Her husband Kang Wei is a longtime business associate who founded Hexi, where Alice Huang previously held an executive role. In 2022, Kang became an executive of Century Longteng, which owns the controlling stake in the Shenzhen data center and he also attended the company's signing of the Huawei agreement.

articles.title_zh: Outlook outage: Microsoft reports 'issues' with Teams and email - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The company posted about the disruptions on social media.
Microsoft reported issues with users' Exchange Online mailboxes and an issue with Microsoft Teams, according to posts on social media Thursday.
"We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas," the company wrote , after first reporting "users experiencing issues when accessing or using Microsoft Teams functionality in North America."
The company initially said the issues involving Exchange Online mailboxes could be due to infrastructure "experiencing elevated load across multiple regions."
Microsoft later clarified, "We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure."
The company said around 4 p.m. Thursday that it believes its latest attempt to fix the issue showed signs of being successful.
"We've validated an alternative service health check method, which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service. We're now applying this change more broadly," Microsoft said in a statement. "We're also preparing automated recovery systems to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to maintain service stability while this change progresses."
Outlook has been down for a few hours as Microsoft attempted to deploy several fixes.
"We've not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact; however, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health," Microsoft previously said. "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service."
Regarding the issues with Microsoft Teams, the company followed up shortly after first reporting the issue, writing, "Our mitigative actions have successfully restored service health and functionality."
Downdetector , which monitors outages, reported issues with both Microsoft Teams and Outlook, among other products on Thursday.
Regarding the issues affecting Exchange Online mailboxes, the company added, "we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
The company continued to provide updates on the potential fix to the mailbox issue on Thursday, and added, "We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

articles.title_orig: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump downplayed the revelations about Huang, who is an influential adviser to the president on artificial intelligence, saying: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it.”
Trump also brushed off a question about whether he now regrets not acting on the intelligence when he was briefed on it, and suggested that he would be happy to take Huang with him on a trip to Asia next week. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody. But, you know, so does everybody else.”
Republican lawmakers have expressed more alarm, asking Huang to give the House foreign affairs and intelligence committees a closed-door briefing next week on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and his relationship with Alice Huang or Huang Le, an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed, who is of no relation to the Nvidia CEO. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.
Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.
The company’s board said in a statement on Sunday that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.
“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.
Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions.
“I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.
The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang was invited to join Trump’s delegation when he traveled to China in May. Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were also invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping and seated at the top table with Trump and China’s president.
Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.
US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.
The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month.
A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.
Nick Robins-Early and Blake Montgomery contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: The planet ‘is being killed’, Greta Thunberg tells Cop31 climate summit
articles.title_zh: The planet ‘is being killed’, Greta Thunberg tells Cop31 climate summit
articles.content_orig:
Swedish activist criticised world governments for their failure to prevent environmental breakdown
The planet is “not dying, it is being killed and we know by who”, said Greta Thunberg , who excoriated world governments for their failure to prevent environmental breakdown in her first appearance at the annual UN climate talks in five years.
Thunberg , 23, the Swedish activist who became famous for heading the school climate strike movement, delivered her stark message to those gathered at the Cop31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, amid the ongoing failure by countries to adequately address the climate crisis.
“It [Earth] is being killed by the very same people thought to come to our rescue,” Thunberg said.
“No one is coming to our rescue. When our human rights are being threatened by states and other institutions, it’s our duty to stand up and be the adult in the room and fight for everyone’s human rights.”
Thunberg, who in recent years has shifted her focus towards other areas such as the conflict in Gaza , linked worsening global heating to other calamities such as war in an appearance alongside activists from Nepal, Canada and Australia.
“We are heading towards a future of more genocides and more ecocides and the complete compromise of our basic rights and where basic necessities become luxuries,” she said.
“It’s more clear than ever in spaces like these that the situation could not be any less under control. The planet is not dying, it is being killed.”
The intervention, on the fourth day of the two-week summit, came as world leaders who travelled to the Mediterranean coastal city delivered their own verdicts on the climate crisis and the faltering progress to address it.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, who was the only G7 leader to attend the talks, said in a speech that the record hot summer in the UK was “not normal”.
“The climate crisis is not a distant threat; it is upon us all now, devastating lives and livelihoods everywhere,” said Burnham, who promised the UK would get to net zero emissions, and backed a proposal for countries to further electrify their economies.
Beth John, a climate justice adviser at Oxfam GB, said Burnham’s appearance “sends a positive signal”. But she added: “Showing up is not enough: a crisis of this scale needs substantive action, not just signals. The real test of climate leadership is delivery, not declarations.”
The electrification goal is one of the main potential promises expected at the talks, which are being jointly presided over by Turkey and Australia. Some countries want the agreement text to specify that the electricity will be derived from clean energy sources.
Campaigners have criticised governments for their slow pace of emissions cuts and for, so far, failing to rally around a phaseout of fossil fuels in the negotiations.
Current policies are set to heat the planet by 2.7C by the end of the century, a report by Climate Action Tracker found on Thursday. The catastrophic rise in temperatures is slightly more than the group expected last year and well above the 1.5C that world leaders have promised.
Thursday was rife with accounts of the harm caused by the climate crisis. Gita Chaudhary, Nepal’s environment minister, recounted the disastrous landslide – caused by a melting glacier – that struck the country in August, claiming more than 1,500 lives.
after newsletter promotion
“We call the catastrophic climate change event we suffered a mountain tsunami,” Chaudhary told the Guardian. “We lost people, we lost lives, we lost property. Nepal is working for rehabilitation, reconstruction and rebuilding the infrastructure. But the communities, the culture, the lives, we cannot revive.”
In the main conference room, a speech by Mohammad Mustafa, the prime minister of Palestine, drew a standing ovation from delegates as he described the environmental impact of the three-year war with Israel.
“Israel’s restrictions on access to land, water and natural resources have compounded Palestine’s climate challenges,” said Mustafa, who spelled out how widespread destruction in Gaza, including to water supplies, sewerage and farmland, had worsened environmental and health risks.
The Turkish hosts of Cop31 have repeatedly accused Israel of genocide and refused to invite the country’s leadership to Antalya. Israel denies that it has committed genocide and insists it has fought a legitimate war to safeguard its own security.
Another country not formally present at the talks is the US, which did not send a delegation. Donald Trump has withdrawn the country from the international climate framework, derided climate science as a “hoax”, and claimed he would not permit any new wind turbines.
This stance earned a rebuke from John Kerry, the former US secretary of state, who has made the trip to Turkey along with 20 Democratic members of Congress and two state governors. “He’s the biggest loser we’ve seen in a long time on all of these issues,” Kerry said of Trump in response to a question from the Guardian.
The crushing midterm election win by the Democrats has raised hopes here at Cop of the US re-engaging on the climate crisis. But Gavin Newsom, the governor of California, warned the final two years of the Trump presidency would not see fundamental change on climate policy.
“I don’t want to romanticise what this will mean,” Newsom said on Thursday. “I don’t expect they’ll do anything but double down.”

articles.title_orig: Nvidia live updates: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, allegations of a third affair emerge
articles.title_zh: Nvidia live updates: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, allegations of a third affair emerge
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a  suspected agent of China and another with an executive who reported to him — a stunning turn of events for the head of a company at the heart of the global AI investment boom.
Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, will become interim CEO, Nvidia’s board said in a statement.
Nvidia shares plunged more as much as 16% after the board’s announcement, before later recovering and trading lower by about 5%. A company spokesperson clarified that Huang will not be working with Nvidia in any capacity going forward.
The company also named its first chairman. That role will be filled by Harvey Jones, who is a former CEO of major chip company Synopsys. The addition of a chairman is a major governance overhaul at a company that for decades relied solely on Huang.
Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to address Huang’s future at the company, a source familiar with the matter told NBC News, adding that the White House was aware of the meeting.
Huang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in the early 1990s and led the company’s meteoric rise amid the AI boom of the past several years.
“I believe deeply in this company and in its future,” Kress wrote in her first email to Nvidia employees as interim CEO. “The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.”
In a separate note to the company’s workforce, Jones, the new chairman, wrote: “The Board takes seriously our duty as stewards of this great company.”
Kress has been the company’s chief financial officer since 2013. She is a familiar face to Wall Street, regularly appearing at conferences and discussing the intricacies of the company’s sprawling operations. Before Nvidia, Kress worked at Cisco, another major technology company, and Microsoft.
Huang long leaned on Kress during financial conferences and the company’s earnings calls to debrief the investing public about the latest developments with the company’s operations.
Nvidia’s board said that it would search for a permanent CEO and consider internal and external candidates.
President Donald Trump weighed in on the search for a permanent CEO shortly after Nvidia’s announcement, saying that Apple executive chair Tim Cook should take the role. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote.
Cook only became Apple’s executive chair on Sept. 1 and did not appear to have plans to leave any time soon.
Kress’ ascension to the CEO role comes after the second largest public company in the world was hit with multiple scandals involving its founder.
On Wednesday, The New York Times , citing five people who worked at Nvidia, reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a married healthcare executive who reported to him, which appears to run afoul of Nvidia’s code of conduct. NBC News has not independently verified the claims.
Nvidia and the executive did not respond to multiple requests for comment Wednesday about the Times’ report.
The report concerning the alleged relationship followed reports that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman believed to be a spy for China. The two Huangs are not related.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a memo to officials in the Trump administration this spring outlining how U.S. intelligence showed that Huang was in a romantic relationship with a business executive who was an asset of China’s spy service, according to a person familiar with Nvidia and a former national security official with knowledge of the matter. The New York Times and the Financial Times , citing people familiar with the matter, first reported on the memo last week.
Alice Huang held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was buying advanced chips from Nvidia. Megaspeed and other related firms remain under U.S. criminal investigation of allegations they smuggled American-made chips into China.
Alice Huang’s precise role and relationship with China’s spy service is unclear. It is possible she was not a career spy for China’s spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, but was asked to cooperate and share information based on her access to Jensen Huang, according to the former national security official.
The concerns about the Nvidia CEO’s extramarital activity added to worries about Nvidia chips being smuggled or illegally accessed by Chinese AI companies. Nvidia has said that it follows U.S. export laws.
On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating whether Huang had fallen victim to a foreign intelligence plot. It said Tuesday that it had hired a former acting U.S. attorney and his law firm to conduct the investigation.
Huang apologized in a memo to employees and said he supported the independent investigation.
“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Multiple Washington officials have called for greater scrutiny of Nvidia and for Huang to testify about his relationship with the suspected Chinese agent in the wake of the reports.
China has denied the allegations, calling them “purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.”
Even before Wednesday’s Times report, Nvidia shares had plunged 11% this week, wiping out nearly $500 billion in paper value. Huang’s departure leaves a host of unknowns at the company, the valuation of which has soared to more than $4 trillion amid insatiable demand for its GPU chips. Those specialized processors underpin the AI applications that have powered the stock market and economic growth writ large to new heights.
For years, Huang has effectively been the chief ambassador for the artificial intelligence industry, appearing regularly alongside heads of state and other CEOs as the industry spends trillions of dollars investing and building AI models and data centers.
Nvidia acknowledged Huang’s contributions to the sector in its Thursday announcement. “Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound,” a statement said. “The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.”
After coming up with the idea for Nvidia at a Denny’s restaurant in Silicon Valley with co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
Before Wednesday’s report of a second affair, many high-profile figures across Silicon Valley, Wall Street and Washington had come to Huang’s defense. Trump told reporters Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country.”
“I think he’s an honorable guy,” Trump said. “I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.”
Shaun Maguire, a partner at the venture capital group Sequoia, said on X that Huang is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” adding that “two mistakes don’t make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.”
SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded under Maguire’s post, writing: “I agree.”
Before the decision, Musk said in a response to a post Wednesday night that it “would be an honor” to hire Huang.
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.
Brian Cheung is a business and data correspondent for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s Ousted CEO, Was the Face of the A.I. Boom Powering the U.S. Economy
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s Ousted CEO, Was the Face of the A.I. Boom Powering the U.S. Economy
articles.content_orig:
As investors have pumped trillions of dollars into artificial intelligence companies, chipmakers and data center developers, the economy has come to rely on the industry as its primary — some would argue only — reliable driver of growth.
No company has been more central to that growth than Nvidia, whose chips fill the data centers that power A.I. and whose money helps to finance them. And, at least until this week, it was impossible to imagine Nvidia without Jensen Huang, its high-flying, leather-clad co-founder and chief executive.
All of which means that Mr. Huang’s resignation on Thursday , following a made-for-Hollywood series of scandals, matters not just for the company and its investors, but for virtually every American.
Or, as Aaron Klein, an expert in financial regulation at the Brookings Institution, put it: “Can one C.E.O.’s sex life take down the economy?”
The answer, in a literal sense, is almost certainly no. No one believes that Mr. Huang’s resignation will, by itself, bring the A.I. boom to an end, let alone plunge the economy into a recession. Nvidia’s stock price tumbled on Thursday , but the broader market barely budged.
But Mr. Klein’s quip spoke to the unique role that Mr. Huang played at Nvidia, and that his company has played in the A.I. build out.

articles.title_orig: Sheinbaum to address APEC business leaders in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
articles.title_zh: Sheinbaum to address APEC business leaders in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
articles.content_orig:
President Sheinbaum’s agenda in China next week was a key focus of today’s mañanera .
Sheinbaum will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting in the southeastern Chinese city of Shenzhen next Wednesday and Thursday.
She announced last week that she will also attend a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
On Thursday morning, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard provided an overview of Sheinbaum’s agenda in China.
He and other cabinet ministers, including Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco, will accompany the president on her trip to China, her first to Asia since she was sworn in on Oct. 1, 2024.
The focus on Sheinbaum’s upcoming trip at today’s mañanera served as a reminder that Mexico has taken a more prominent place on the international stage under her leadership than it occupied during Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s presidency. AMLO only took seven international trips during his six-year term, a number matched by Sheinbaum before she reached the two-year milestone of her presidency .
In addition to attending the APEC meeting in China next week, Sheinbaum will also travel to Florida next month to attend the G20 Leaders’ Summit. At today’s mañanera , she said that her first formal face-to-face meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump could take place at the latter event.
Ebrard told reporters that Sheinbaum will have official activities scheduled in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 19.
He noted that Shenzhen is considered the technology capital of China.
“That’s why they proposed holding [the APEC meeting] there,” Ebrard said.
He announced that Sheinbaum will be the main speaker at an APEC Business Advisory Council event to be held in Shenzhen next week. Ebrard said that the council is made up of “more than 1,000 businesspeople from the 21 [APEC] countries.”
“We think that this is the most important [business] forum for … the Asia-Pacific [region] and our president is going to play a very important role,” he said.
“She will be one of the few heads of state that will address the group in the plenary session,” Ebrard said.
In fact, just Sheinbaum and Xi will address the session attended by all members of the APEC Business Advisory Council, he said.
Ebrard also announced that Sheinbaum will hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of various APEC countries, including those of China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam. He said that other APEC countries have requested bilateral meetings with Mexico, and that it is “very likely” they will take place. Ebrard said that leaders of APEC countries have significant interest in “talking to the president and Mexico.”
He said that Sheinbaum will also participate in the APEC Leaders’ Meeting. Ebrard noted that the theme of this year’s meeting is “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.”
He subsequently told reporters that 52% of foreign direct investment in Mexico comes from APEC countries. Ebrard also noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028.
Later in the press conference, Sheinbaum told reporters that she won’t hold a bilateral meeting with Trump during her visit to China next week.
She said she would “probably” meet with the U.S. president during the G20 Leaders’ Summit at the Mar-A-Lago Club in Florida in December.
“We will seek … [a bilateral meeting] if the opportunity arises,” Sheinbaum said.
She emphasized that there is constant communication between Mexico and the United States on trade issues.
Sheinbaum said last week that she was interested in meeting with Trump in China.
Sheinbaum told reporters that she will speak about Plan México — the federal government’s ambitious economic plan — at the APEC Business Advisory Council event.
“We’re going to talk about Plan México, about what we’ve done , about what our country’s economic model means,” she said.
Sheinbaum wants to make Mexico 10th largest economy in the world with ‘Plan México’
Sheinbaum said she will also speak to businesspeople about how they can invest in Mexico.
Among the goals of Plan México are to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and to increase the use of national content in products made in Mexico’s large manufacturing sector.
“The objective of Plan Mexico is to produce more in Mexico and import less,” Sheinbaum told reporters.
Sheinbaum told reporters that there is no reason why her meeting with Xi should affect Mexico’s trade negotiations with the United States.
“That we’re going to have a meeting with the president of China shouldn’t be a problem in the trade agreement negotiations with the United States,” she said.
Mexico and the United States have been seeking to resolve a range of trade differences after the Trump administration announced in July that it had decided against renewing the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years to 2042.
The United States’ concerns include its large trade deficit with Mexico , Mexico’s trade relationship with China and Mexico’s energy sector rules . Mexico is seeking a reduction, if not the elimination, of U.S. tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles.

articles.title_orig: Mortgage Rates Remain High as Affordability Challenges Persist
articles.title_zh: Mortgage Rates Remain High as Affordability Challenges Persist
articles.content_orig:
Mortgage rates slid for the fourth consecutive week but remain above 7 percent, adding pressure to a bleak housing market struggling with rising prices and declining sales.
The rate on the most popular home loan in the United States, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, fell slightly to 7.11 percent, from 7.18 percent the week before, the mortgage finance giant Freddie Mac said on Thursday. The same rate averaged 6.24 percent a year ago.
There was hope that mortgage rates might ease below 7 percent, a psychological threshold that could draw more buyers to the market. But industry experts say that marker is not likely to be breached any time soon.
High housing costs have made buying a home unaffordable for many Americans, said Brad Case, the chief residential economist at Homes.com, a real estate search portal owned by CoStar, a data analytics company.
“I don’t think affordability challenges are going away any time soon,” he added, “because I don’t think we’re likely to see substantially lower mortgage rates.”
Squeezed by high mortgage rates and rising inflation, buyers and sellers are sitting out of the market until conditions improve, which has depressed home sales. Sales of existing homes fell 8.8 percent in October from the year before, and 5.5 percent lower than September’s pace, according to a report released Thursday by the National Association of Realtors, a trade group.

articles.title_orig: How a 24-year-old built a $37 million media empire by asking billionaires for advice
articles.title_zh: How a 24-year-old built a $37 million media empire by asking billionaires for advice
articles.content_orig:
James Dumoulin, co-founder of The School of Hard Knocks, joins 'The Big Money Show' to discuss building his multimillion-dollar media brand through street interviews with successful entrepreneurs.
At a time when headlines frequently focus on younger Americans embracing "quiet quitting" and demanding lighter workloads, 24-year-old James Dumoulin is flipping the script.
As the co-founder of the viral media brand School of Hard Knocks, Dumoulin built a $37 million media empire with more than 26 million followers by hitting the pavement, overcoming fear and talking directly to the world's most successful business leaders.
"One of my favorite sayings is that, where attention goes, revenue flows," Dumoulin said during an appearance on "The Big Money Show" Thursday. "If you want to go fast, go by yourself. If you wanna go further and go big, you gotta go with people together."
The young entrepreneur and social media personality explained how he started the brand with his brother and childhood friend. Rather than relying solely on the unpredictability of digital advertising revenue, Dumoulin said they diversified their portfolio and now operate four distinct business ventures.
YOUNG MILLIONAIRE REVEALS THE WEALTH-BUILDING LESSONS HE LEARNED FROM BILLIONAIRES
"Logan Paul told me, ‘You have to know how to yield that attention into actual businesses.’ So we got really intentional about ‘Why do people follow us?’ And we decided to build businesses off of that and built really smart businesses, hired great people," Dumoulin reflected.
School Of Hard Knocks co-founder and influencer James Dumoulin visits Fox Business Network Studios July 15, 2025. (Getty Images)
According to Forbes , Dumoulin ranks No. 37 on its 2026 list of top content creators, with estimated earnings of $9.9 million.
"We built a huge audience. … But then you've got to think a little bit bigger. … We're spending so much time around wealthy entrepreneurs. … So, we built a marketing agency to help them build their personal brands. We launched a content consulting company, and then we launched a subscription community where every week we host live calls," he explained.
"So, people think that we just do interviews, and we run up to people like Marcus [Lemonis] on the street. I have four businesses that are doing seven or eight figures at 24 years old."
The brand's trajectory changed after Dumoulin approached Mark Cuban for a spontaneous interview. Since then, he has interviewed 70 billionaires, including Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, whom he recently traveled to Nigeria to interview.
Dumoulin says he secures these high-profile interviews through a straightforward approach of prioritizing long-term relationships and mutual benefit over sensationalized sound bites.
"Take the risk or lose the chance. Had I not gone up to Mark Cuban, had I gotten hesitant and was afraid to approach him, I wouldn't have been able to leverage that now," he reflected. "But my message is very simple: The odds of us all sitting here, being born, everybody watching this is 1 in 400 trillion. You were obviously created for a reason. I'm a firm believer that people watching this were born to do more than go to school and get a job, pay bills and die.
"So, like, you might as well go for it. You might as well get really intentional and in tune about what was that reason why you were created, what that purpose is and become the absolute best in the world at it.
"I make it very clear to people whenever I'm about to do an interview with them, there's no curveballs. … I don't value the two minutes of fame. Our platform's big enough now. I don't want to put anybody in a bad light."
James Dumoulin, co-founder of School of Hard Knocks, shares his journey to financial success, explaining how his media company, with millions of followers, monetizes access to top entrepreneurs.
The best piece of advice Dumoulin said he has received came from former Goodyear executive Billy Ray Taylor, who shared a lesson from his mother.
GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE
"He said, ‘If a bird lands on a branch, does the bird trust the branch or does it trust its wings?" Dumoulin shared. "I've seen many birds land on branches, but what I've never seen is the branch break and the bird fall and die. Trust your wings.
"So, I think that I really lean heavily on that because, especially once you start to get a little bit of traction, a little of motion, you have all these people telling you, ‘You need to run your business that way, this way, this way, this way.’ And, ultimately, you gotta keep the main thing the main thing."

articles.title_orig: Stocks Slide on Nvidia Troubles, Oil Edges Lower: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks Slide on Nvidia Troubles, Oil Edges Lower: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s shares plummeted Thursday, sending tremors through global markets, as the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang , stepped down from his role.
Shares in Nvidia dropped as much as 14 percent when markets opened for trading on Thursday, extending a decline that has wiped out more than $1 trillion from the company’s market value this month alone. The stock began to reverse most of its losses by late morning.
The broader market rose slightly, too, as investors began to conclude that the fallout of Mr. Jensen’s departure would not fundamentally undermine the artificial intelligence trade. Yields on the 10-year U.S. Treasury rose above 5 percent on Thursday for the first time in weeks. Yields go up when Treasury prices go down.
Nvidia has emerged as central to the A.I. economy because its chips — or graphic processing units — help train and power models across the industry. It has also become a central bank of sorts for several A.I. companies, because its finances are deeply intertwined with those of everyone from frontier A.I. labs to neoclouds, which rent out computing power.
“This is an Nvidia problem before it is an A.I. problem,” said Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial. But he added that Nvidia’s woes could trickle through to other companies.
“Where I would be careful is with the smaller A.I. cloud companies that leaned on Nvidia’s checkbook,” he said. “If the new regime gets more conservative about financing its own customers, that is where it shows up first.”

articles.title_orig: Why Trump thinks tiny trucks could solve car affordability crisis
articles.title_zh: Why Trump thinks tiny trucks could solve car affordability crisis
articles.content_orig:
Imagine a pickup truck, but much smaller, lighter and lacking any frills. It’s a vehicle that people in Japan have been using for decades. And now Toyota wants to sell one in the United States.
This week, the automaker introduced a tiny pickup truck inspired by Japanese “Kei” trucks, under the Scion brand that Toyota shuttered in 2016. The vehicle, the Scion KEI-01, will go on sale next year.
Kei vehicles (pronounced like the letter “K”) are a distinct category of small cars, vans and trucks in Japan and other Asian countries. These vehicles have long had a cult following in the United States. Even President Trump showed adoration , calling them “really cute” and “sort of like the Beetle used to be.” He made the remarks last year after a visit to Japan and mused about finding a way to have them sold in the United States.
But buying and using one of these vehicles in the United States is not easy. Car buffs who want Kei cars and trucks typically import vehicles that are at least 25 years old from Japan to take advantage of a provision in U.S. law that exempts older vehicles from federal safety and emissions standards.
Toyota says the KEI-01 will be assembled in Indiana and will qualify as a “low speed vehicle” under federal regulations. Vehicles in that category must have a top speed of 25 miles an hour and are generally forbidden from roads with speed limits of more than 35 m.p.h. Such vehicles also do not have to meet the same safety and other standards as regular cars.
The KEI-01 is in many ways the opposite of traditional U.S. pickup trucks like the Ford F-150 or Chevrolet Silverado, which over the past several decades have become bigger, heavier and more expensive. Most automakers have found that it is much easier to make a profit on larger vehicles because they tend not to cost much more to make than smaller ones but can be sold for a lot more money.

articles.title_orig: Is Outlook down? Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.title_zh: Is Outlook down? Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.content_orig:
CHICAGO — A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps.
As of around 1:30 p.m. ET, more than 120,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook — with many saying they couldn’t send and receive emails, or encountering delays. Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft said that it was investigating.
In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”
Microsoft later added that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company said it would begin ”redistributing” traffic to help balance the load.
Microsoft did not immediately provide further information. Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.
